title: Polynomial-time production of packed records
statement: For every finite-state Boolean Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e,c,A,d$, there are a finite-state Boolean Turing machine $H$ and natural numbers $a,r$ such that $H$ computes the function sending each word $x$ to its packed records within $a(|x|+1)^r$ steps, and the resulting word has length at most $a(|x|+1)^r$ for every $x$.
replaced: For every source machine and parameters, there are a machine and constants $a, r$ such that the machine computes the complete packed preparation data within $a(n+1)^r$ steps on inputs of length $n$, and the packed answer itself has length at most the same bound.
